speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you have a psychiatric condition and a new onset movement disorder; to help me understand your situation, please describe your symptoms, how long they have been present, and what medications or treatments you have been taking.

speaker: Patient
text: 23-year-old college student. The patient is here for a follow-up appointment. He was recently diagnosed with schizophrenia and started on risperidone approximately 2 months ago. Reports a significant improvement in psychiatric symptoms since the start of treatment.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is good news regarding your psychiatric improvement. However, since you are here for a new movement disorder, when did you first notice these motor symptoms, and how would you describe them?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Inability to remain still, persistent feeling of restlessness. I also have Frequent fidgeting, Repetitive crossing and uncrossing of legs, Pacing.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Drug-Induced Akathisia.

The symptoms you describe—inability to remain still, persistent restlessness, and pacing—are classic signs of akathisia, a common side effect of antipsychotic medications like risperidone. I am confident in this diagnosis based on your history and current presentation.
